notes: Evaluation set derived from the paper. Numbering follows the project brief (list starts at 4). Questions 1-3 were appended in Phase 5 covering the abstract/introduction (pages 1-2); the file now reports 18 questions.

questions.question: What framework does the paper introduce, and how is it described relative to the LLM-as-a-Judge framework?
questions.expected_answer: The Agent-as-a-Judge framework, described as an organic extension of LLM-as-a-Judge that uses agentic systems to evaluate agentic systems.

questions.question: Where is the DevAI dataset hosted according to the paper's metadata?
According to the introduction, what percentage alignment with the consensus of human judges did Agent-as-a-Judge and LLM-as-a-Judge each achieve?
questions.expected_answer: Agent-as-a-Judge aligned with 90% of the human-judge consensus, compared to 70% for LLM-as-a-Judge.

questions.question: What is the DevAI dataset, and how many tasks, requirements, and preferences does it contain?
questions.expected_answer: DevAI is the AI Developer Dataset with 55 tasks, 365 hierarchical requirements, and 125 preferences.

questions.question: What percentage of evaluation time and cost does Agent-as-a-Judge save compared to using three human experts?
questions.expected_answer: 97.72% of evaluation time and 97.64% of evaluation cost.

questions.question: According to Section 4.4 (Cost Analysis), how much did Agent-as-a-Judge cost and how long did it take, compared to Human-as-a-Judge?
questions.expected_answer: Agent-as-a-Judge: $30.58 and 118.43 minutes; Human-as-a-Judge: $1,297.50 and 86.5 hours.

questions.question: Which three open-source agentic frameworks were benchmarked on DevAI?
What is the average cost and average time for OpenHands?
questions.expected_answer: Average cost is $6.38 and average time is 362.41 seconds.

questions.question: Which system is the most cost-efficient and which is the most expensive?
questions.expected_answer: MetaGPT is the most cost-efficient ($1.19 average); OpenHands is the most expensive ($6.38 average).

questions.question: What was GPT-Pilot's "Requirements Met (Independent)" percentage under Human-as-a-Judge?
What was MetaGPT's Task Solve Rate?
In the black-box setting, what Alignment Rate did Agent-as-a-Judge vs. LLM-as-a-Judge achieve when evaluating OpenHands?
What alignment rate does Agent-as-a-Judge achieve using only the "ask" component, and after adding "graph," "read," and "locate"?
Which search algorithm (BM25, Sentence-BERT, Fuzzy Search, or no search module) gave the best alignment rate?
questions.expected_answer: Removing the search module gave the best rate (90.44%); BM25 86.06%, Sentence-BERT 87.70%, Fuzzy Search 85.52%.

questions.question: Which two model architectures are mentioned most frequently in the DevAI user queries?
What is requirement R1 in the "Devin AI Software Engineer Plants Secret Messages in Images" task?
questions.expected_answer: R1: Ensure the generated images are of 1080p resolution and saved in results/.

questions.question: Which of the three human evaluators (231a, 38bb, cn9o) made the most errors when judging GPT-Pilot, and what was the error rate?
questions.expected_answer: cn9o, with a 23.77% error rate on GPT-Pilot.

questions.question: In the diagram comparing LLM-as-a-Judge, Agent-as-a-Judge, and Human-as-a-Judge, what key drawback is highlighted for Human-as-a-Judge?
questions.expected_answer: Human evaluation is time-consuming and requires substantial manual effort and expertise.
